title: Lucknow Pact and Bengal Implications
subtitle: The Congress–Muslim League agreement of December 1916 accepted separate electorates and allocated Muslims 40% of Bengal council seats.
summary: At their December 1916 sessions in Lucknow, the Indian National Congress and All-India Muslim League adopted a joint constitutional scheme known as the Lucknow Pact. Congress accepted separate electorates, while the agreed provincial formula allotted Muslims 40 percent of Bengal’s legislative seats despite their majority in the province. This underrepresentation drew criticism from some Bengal Muslim leaders; Bengal responses were not uniform. The available catalog sources establish the broad constitutional context but do not adequately document the local debate or its actors.
heroTagline: A national agreement whose seat formula drew criticism in Muslim-majority Bengal.
whyItMatters: The Bengal allocation illustrates the pact’s compromise: cross-party agreement on minority safeguards elsewhere came with Muslim underrepresentation in Bengal. A chapter promising the pact’s Bengal implications needs stronger, Bengal-specific scholarship on the negotiations, local criticism, and subsequent political effects; the current catalog cannot support that fuller account.
